column1: # ALREADY SATISFY `cond` — keys preserved for a map, order for a list.
# "Already satisfies" is the meet CHANGING NOTHING, not mere
# unifiability. A map is open, so `{p:2}` unifies with `{debug:true}`
# by gaining the key, and a filter that kept everything that could be
# made to match would keep everything — the first row is the case that
# settles it. The design named unifiability; its own example is
# unsatisfiable under it (see the register, G8.2 departures).
# The condition is an ordinary value, so the constraint atoms compose
# with it for free — `min(2)`, `{x:min(2)}` — and a failing child is an
# THE SAME LENGTH RULE, from the other side. `filter(bag, [])` keeps
# only the elements that unify with the empty tuple, which is none of

# its trial meet never set the flag the length gate reads (BUGS.md
